- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp negative swings, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior), model frequently lags — adjust forecast to anticipate the spike 1–2 days ahead.  
- If model forecast is flat or trending upward with no sentiment support, it often fails to capture mean reversion — reduce forecast slope slightly to reflect volatility.  
- In periods of high sentiment volatility (alternating 0.67/0.00/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.  
- If true outcome is significantly below model (e.g., >5% drop), model may be overconfident — apply downward bias of 1–3% based on sentiment decay.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates long-term mean reversion — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
